correctness.rationale: The copula maximum law is \(G_M=\Delta\circ F\). The published diagonal characterization makes \(\Delta\) absolutely continuous with derivative \(q\in[0,d]\) almost everywhere and mean one. Differentiating the composition gives \(g_M/f=q\circ F\); convexity is equivalent to a nondecreasing derivative representative, exactly the likelihood-ratio condition. The divergence identity follows from the probability-integral transform, while Jensen and the endpoint chord bound give the sharp envelope. Boundary and independence cases were recomputed directly.

value.rationale: The result gives a probabilistic interpretation to the convex-diagonal dependence class used in recent sharp anti-concentration theory: it is exactly maximum-to-margin likelihood-ratio dominance. This is a structural characterization, not a parameter rewrite. The linked margin-free divergence identity and sharp dimension-only envelope quantify the information separation between a coordinate and the maximum and identify exact extremal diagonals.
